title: Add a small discover-and-compromise loop before automation
evidence: _handle_click routes tools directly to placement, and _try_place_node pays resources and creates an owned node immediately. Unowned map blocks have no host discovery or compromise state. The accepted discovery direction is future work, not a missing implemented requirement.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: choose a producer, click valid ground, then draw its tunnel; no target assessment occurs.
impact: The player's main decision reads as building a producer rather than gaining access to a hostile endpoint.
recommendation: Prototype one starter chain: inspect a nearby host, see yield/security, deploy a foothold, then keep the existing tunnel and packet automation.
acceptance: A first-time player can identify a host and deliberately acquire it within five minutes; pause planning, existing costs, shape cues and automatic production remain usable.

title: Make compromised hosts look acquired rather than newly constructed
evidence: STRUCT supplies roof, windows, tiers and height for player nodes; _draw_building constructs architecture over the static city. The same physical-building metaphor dominates both unowned and owned map objects.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: compare _paint_city background blocks with the tier/roof rendering of a deployed producer.
impact: Neon decoration does not clearly communicate the change from remote target to controlled host.
recommendation: Keep the city backdrop and footprint, but present acquired endpoints as marked hosts or executable modules with an unmistakable compromised state and resource glyph.
acceptance: Before/after ownership can be identified at normal and far zoom without relying on colour; High Contrast and Reduced Motion preserve the cue.

title: Give important commands a short persistent operations history
evidence: Most actions replace the single main.message string, including deployment, links, commands, contracts and ICE events. There is no event history connecting multiple player commands to their outcomes.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: deploy, connect, and overclock in sequence; each success replaces the previous message.
impact: Successful operations feel like configuration changes and their causal sequence is easy to lose.
recommendation: Keep three recent high-value command acknowledgements and a brief target-local cue for foothold/session success. Do not log routine packets.
acceptance: Deployment, session establishment and ICE evasion remain reviewable after another action; the feed stays bounded and readable at 200% text.

title: Teach a sustainable Cycles backbone before expanding Intel sales
evidence: _next_step asks for a Phishing Kit before checking any Cycles source. has_producer includes Intel producers, so its later producer check cannot teach Cycles sustainability. Tunnels deduct upkeep from the starting 80 Cycles.
reproduction: Start with only C2: evaluate _next_step, then add a linked Phishing Kit and Market without a compute producer.
impact: A new player is directed into an unsustainable network before being taught the economy that keeps packets moving.
recommendation: Add a compact first-steps sequence that checks connected Cycles income and upkeep before requesting the Intel-to-Market chain.
acceptance: Fresh-start guidance requests a productive linked Cycles host; once sustained, it advances to Intel and Cash, and returns to recovery advice if Cycles income stops.

title: Validate an accessible starter route for each generated map
evidence: _place_hub selects the first residential coarse cell from the left. Generation does not validate reachable legal producer footprints, nearby Intel access, or the cost of the first useful reveal route.
reproduction: Source review of generation and hub placement; inspect a fixed seed set for legal starter Cycles/Intel paths and required spend.
impact: Procedural variation can change the cost and clarity of the first lesson before the player understands routing; frequency needs a seed sweep, not a claimed played failure.
recommendation: Validate a small opening neighbourhood and reroll or adjust only invalid starts, preserving the rest of the random city.
acceptance: A documented seed batch always offers a legal Cycles foothold and an affordable path toward Intel using starting resources and early income.

title: Separate victory progress from the wallet spent on upgrades
evidence: The win check uses resources.credits >= 1000, while advanced facilities and tunnels deduct that same wallet. Every investment immediately reduces displayed goal progress even when it improves the network.
reproduction: At a high Cash balance, buy a Cloud Cryptojacker, Mixer or HTTP tunnel; the victory balance falls by its cost.
impact: Near the finish, waiting with an adequate network can be more appealing than using the unlocked construction choices.
recommendation: Evaluate a cumulative earned-Cash milestone or a one-time final operation funded from Cash; keep Cash as the spendable currency.
acceptance: A successful upgrade does not erase completed objective progress, and the goal clearly communicates whether earnings, retained balance or a final spend is required.

title: Give the central Spire a simple end-of-run purpose
evidence: Generation always creates a Spire with ICE tier 3, but ZONE_RES gives it no output and victory checks only the Cash balance. It provides no unique operation or completion condition.
reproduction: Compare the Spire's generation/security entries with _placement_error, producer resource mappings and the win check.
impact: The visually prominent centre promises a destination that the economy does not require the player to reach.
recommendation: Add one optional or final Spire operation using existing Tools, routing and Cash rather than adding a separate progression currency.
acceptance: The Spire has a stated actionable purpose and visible completion result; a player can understand its requirements before committing to the route.

title: Allow players to replay and share a map seed
evidence: The main menu assigns randi() for every New Game. Session.seed is already consumed by main and the current seed is available in Stats, but there is no seed-entry or restart-same-seed action.
reproduction: Source walkthrough of New Game and Session.seed consumption; the current menu always selects a new random seed.
impact: Players cannot easily retry a difficult layout, compare routing solutions or reproduce an interesting city.
recommendation: Offer an optional seed field and a restart-this-map action; retain random New Game as the default.
acceptance: Entering the same seed produces the same layout and start, and the chosen seed can be copied without accessing save files.

title: Permit a small set of producer upgrades that preserve the route
evidence: Higher-tier producers are separate placement tools. Replacing an existing footprint requires removal, and _remove_node detaches its incoming children and destroys their out-links.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: replace a routing producer with a stronger same-resource producer; removal detaches connected child links.
impact: Research offers more production choices, but adopting them can demand repeated rewiring instead of improving an established network.
recommendation: Support only obvious same-resource upgrades, charge the upgrade cost, and preserve footprint, parent route and incoming links when compatible.
acceptance: An upgraded Cycles or Intel host retains valid network connections, recalculates load/output, and remains reversible through the existing undo model.

title: Tie coverage yield to suitable hosts instead of every nearby building
evidence: _coverage counts any eligible city building inside the disk. _production applies the same multiplier to all producer types without checking the covered block's service or resource.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: compare two producer types placed near the same occupied blocks; both receive the same density multiplier.
impact: Every hack optimises the same geometric building count, weakening the meaning of package registries, mail hosts and cloud targets.
recommendation: When host discovery is introduced, count suitable discovered target classes or apply one clear host affinity; keep the same output resource and radius.
acceptance: Two hack types can have a readable reason to prefer different targets, with eligible coverage visible before commitment and no extra resource type.

title: Give Crypto laundering a return profile distinct from Intel sales
evidence: When a processor creates credits, _move_packets applies _market_price regardless of processor type. The Crypto Mixer therefore suffers the same wallet-based saturation as the Darknet Market, although _next_step recommends diversification.
reproduction: Source calculation: a Mixer credit return and a Market credit return at the same Cash balance both receive the same price multiplier.
impact: The expensive Crypto branch changes inputs but does not provide a different answer to falling Intel sale prices.
recommendation: Evaluate a simple distinct laundering payout or saturation curve, or present Crypto honestly as an alternate supply source rather than relief from Intel saturation.
acceptance: The Crypto branch has a documented economic niche demonstrated against a same-cost Intel expansion at mid-to-late Cash balances.

title: Make Onion Routing's long-reach promise measurable
evidence: All five TUNNEL_MAXLEN entries equal 255. Onion Routing is described as long-reach but currently differs through loss/upkeep/capacity rather than a larger routing budget.
reproduction: Compare _tool_maxlen for DNS, VPN, Reverse Shell, HTTP and Onion; all return the same maximum route length.
impact: The advanced unlock does not communicate a clearly distinct reach capability, so a costly Tool-based purchase can disappoint the stated expectation.
recommendation: Give Onion one clear distance niche, such as a larger route budget or strongly improved long-route economics, and describe that exact benefit.
acceptance: A documented route comparison demonstrates a useful Onion advantage that another early protocol does not already provide at lower total cost.

title: Stop optional Labs consuming inputs after the last useful unlock
evidence: TECH contains a finite seven-entry tree. _sim_tick continues Lab pulls and fuel spending after all technologies are researched; Research has no further spend in the current game.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: mark all TECH entries researched, retain an enabled linked Lab with Intel and Cycles, then evaluate processor pulls.
impact: A completed research system can keep diverting the resources needed for the remaining Cash objective without producing usable value.
recommendation: Put Labs in automatic standby when no current Research spend remains, with an explicit resume option for continued sandbox stockpiling.
acceptance: After the last unlock, ordinary Lab automation stops consuming Intel/Cycles and clearly reports standby; manual override and saves preserve the intended state.

title: Make starter compute Overclock economics understandable
evidence: Overclock costs 20 Cycles for 20 seconds. A 1.0 coverage Mirai adds 20 gross Cycles before route loss; on a 10-cell DNS route its expected extra delivery is 17 Cycles, below the cost.
reproduction: Source expectation calculation using RATE_NEST=1, multiplier=1, duration=20 and DNS distance loss=10*0.015; this is an expected return, not a played sample.
impact: The first available compute boost can appear to be a recovery tool while worsening the player's Cycles reserve.
recommendation: Show its expected gain and loss, or tune starter-compute cost/duration so an uncongested sustainable route has a clear positive benefit.
acceptance: The command communicates whether extra delivered output is expected to exceed its cost; a starter recovery use has a documented useful case.

title: Make going quiet a meaningful answer to escalating pursuit
evidence: notoriety uses max(previous, wealth)+0.03 per second, never decays, and can independently charge sweeps above 45 even when Trace is zero. DDoS resets Trace and charge but not notoriety.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: once notoriety exceeds 45, use silent DNS/VPN links and zero Trace; _update_sweep still accumulates pursuit charge.
impact: Quiet protocol choices eventually stop preventing pursuit, while the game's guidance frames quieting as a defensive response.
recommendation: Either let sustained low exposure reduce pursuit pressure, or explicitly teach that permanent reputation requires active evasion rather than quieting.
acceptance: A low-exposure strategy has a documented effect on future sweep frequency, or the independent reputation threat is clearly introduced before it becomes irreversible.

title: Choose ICE entry points using exposure as well as path depth
evidence: _launch_sweep picks the connected node with the largest _chain length. It does not consider protocol noise, valuable output, active production or the origin of current Trace.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: compare a long silent chain with a short noisy branch; the longest chain wins target selection regardless of exposure.
impact: Building a deep efficient backbone determines the target more strongly than risky hacking decisions, reducing the strategic relevance of protocol choice.
recommendation: Use a small deterministic exposure score with depth as a tie-breaker and identify the implicated branch in the warning.
acceptance: A documented network example shows that increased exposure changes the entry target predictably without making the warning harder to read or removing pause-safe counterplay.

title: Allow unwanted contract offers to rotate out
evidence: The board stops generation at three contracts. Deadlines decrease only for accepted contracts; an unaccepted offer has no decline or expiry path and can occupy its slot forever.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: let three offers arrive and leave all unaccepted; generation remains blocked indefinitely.
impact: One poor early assortment can suppress later jobs unless the player accepts an unwanted timed task simply to clear it.
recommendation: Add a low-friction decline or replace-offer action, or expire unaccepted offers after a generous separate lifetime.
acceptance: Three unwanted offers cannot permanently block the board, and refreshing offers does not erase an accepted job's progress.

title: Gate early offers to achievable resource chains
evidence: _gen_contract can choose Crypto stock from the first offer; no eligibility check examines research, accessible vaults, Tools or the ability to pay for a Skimmer. The first offer arrives after 10 seconds.
reproduction: Source walkthrough: generate a stock contract at the fresh starting state; Crypto remains an equally selectable stock resource despite the unbuilt guarded supply chain.
impact: Early jobs can advertise an attractive reward for a production path that the player cannot reasonably establish within its deadline.
recommendation: Filter starter offers by currently available or imminently affordable production, allowing advanced offers once their chain is demonstrated.
acceptance: Opening offers have a feasible documented route using available tools/resources; advanced Crypto jobs appear after the relevant production path becomes attainable.

title: Account for route latency and supply rate in contract difficulty
evidence: Stock, node and Cash jobs use fixed 90/120/100-second deadlines with random quantities. Generation does not consider current income, slow_factor, missing research or packet travel time.
reproduction: Source comparison: the same 50-Intel/90-second contract can be offered to a short sustained route and a distant starved route without changing difficulty or reward.
impact: The contract challenge can be dominated by seed geography and travel time rather than a deliberate player improvement.
recommendation: Use a few simple contract tiers keyed to achieved production, with a travel allowance and clear risk classification; keep acceptance optional.
acceptance: Each tier has a feasible reference network, and the allowed time includes the first required packet round trip without relying on an unimplemented supply chain.

title: Align coverage tuning with the actual radius-four grid ceiling
evidence: A radius-four integer disk intersects at most seven distinct 3x3 occupied blocks on a four-cell grid across all 16 centre phases. Thus current coverage/5 tops out at 1.4 before vacancies/farm narrowing, while the clamp/comment allow 2.5.
reproduction: Read findings/coverage_geometry.json: exhaustive fully occupied-grid upper-bound calculation reproduces _coverage disk and block layout; no Godot playthrough is claimed.
impact: The advertised tuning range above 1.4 is unreachable in the current geometry, which distorts balance assumptions for advanced production and placement rewards.
recommendation: Choose an attainable density reference divisor or lower the documented/tuned upper range; avoid enlarging the radius solely to justify an old number.
acceptance: The stated production multiplier range is reachable on a documented legal dense placement and verified by a small seed sample; sparse placements remain useful.
